extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA
extraction.description: A challenging dataset for commonsense question answering containing 12,247 multiple-choice questions. Questions are authored by crowd-workers based on subgraphs from ConceptNet where multiple target concepts share the same semantic relation to a source concept, encouraging questions that require prior commonsense knowledge beyond simple associations.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Subgraphs each containing one source concept and three target concepts with the same relation were extracted from ConceptNet. Amazon Mechanical Turk crowd-workers authored three questions per subgraph (discriminating between the target concepts), chose one additional distractor from ConceptNet, and manually authored another distractor. A disjoint group of crowd-workers verified question quality. Additionally, textual context was collected by retrieving the first 100 Google search result snippets for each of the five candidate answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ConceptNet knowledge base and web search snippets retrieved via Google search
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: ConceptNet triplets were filtered by: (1) removing general relations (e.g., RelatedTo) or well-explored relations (e.g., IsA), retaining 22 relations; (2) removing triplets where a concept is longer than four words or not in English; (3) removing triplets where the edit distance between source and target concepts is too low. For question verification, questions were filtered out if not verified by at least one worker answering correctly (filtering 15% of formulated questions).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk saw a question concept and three answer concepts sharing a relation, and authored three questions containing the question concept such that only one target concept is the answer. Workers were instructed to avoid strong surface clues. Workers then selected one additional distractor from ConceptNet sharing the same relation and manually wrote one plausible distractor. A separate validation task had workers annotate whether the question is unanswerable or pick the correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question was verified by 2 workers; questions were retained only if at least one verifier answered correctly, filtering out 15% of the questions. Only question formulators whose questions passed verification at least 75% of the time were accepted.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 122 formulators contributed to question generation, but 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions. A disjoint group of workers performed verification.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Reporting bias in web text; potential annotation artifacts and distributional biases; concentration of question authoring where 10 workers created over 85% of the questions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Models that learn from the dataset can struggle when question concepts overlap between training and test splits with different answers; models face difficulties with negation, antonyms, conjunctions, factoid knowledge, and differing granularity between answers and distractors.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of question answering and natural language understanding models on commonsense reasoning.
